01


**TL;DR**


- Is a virtual IBAN the same as a real bank account? No—an identifier does not establish account ownership.
- Virtual IBANs help identify incoming payments; the underlying account determines where funds are held.
- Check the account holder, payment permissions, and protection arrangement before using a virtual IBAN for treasury.
- Infinite serves global businesses needing multicurrency accounts and cross-border payment routing; confirm the specific account structure before choosing.


02


## Is a virtual IBAN the same as a real bank account?


**A virtual IBAN identifies a payment destination; a bank account establishes an account relationship.** Those functions can work together, but they are not interchangeable. A provider can assign distinct virtual IBANs to customers while directing receipts to an underlying collection account.


The word *virtual* does not mean the details are fake. The distinction is whether your business holds a separate account or receives an identifier associated with another account structure. If your main requirement is holding different currencies, start with the separate question of[holding multiple currency accounts under one entity](https://infinite.net/learn/insights/can-a-business-hold-multiple-currency-accounts-under-one-entity) .


**What does it provide?**


- Virtual IBAN arrangement: An identifier linked to an underlying account arrangement
- Directly held bank account: An account relationship with a bank


**Who holds the account?**


- Virtual IBAN arrangement: Depends on the arrangement; obtain written confirmation
- Directly held bank account: The customer named in the bank’s agreement


**Where is the balance recorded?**


- Virtual IBAN arrangement: Potentially in the provider’s customer ledger against underlying funds
- Directly held bank account: In the customer’s bank account records


**What is the main benefit?**


- Virtual IBAN arrangement: Assigning receipts to customers, invoices, or business units
- Directly held bank account: Holding and transacting through an account in the customer’s name


**What is the limitation?**


- Virtual IBAN arrangement: The identifier alone proves neither ownership nor functionality
- Directly held bank account: Account ownership does not guarantee every payment service


**Best for**


- Virtual IBAN arrangement: Separating collection identifiers without assuming separate accounts
- Directly held bank account: Businesses that require a direct bank account relationship


Neither column establishes deposit protection automatically. That depends on the institution, jurisdiction, account structure, and applicable eligibility rules.


03


## Why this matters


Your customers can successfully send money to an IBAN while your business still lacks the account relationship your finance team expects. The discrepancy becomes important when you need proof of account ownership, a bank statement for another provider, or documentation showing how customer funds are held.


For a 2026 banking review, separate operational usefulness from legal status. A virtual IBAN can simplify reconciliation without giving you a separate deposit account. A directly held bank account can establish ownership without supplying the collection identifiers your operations need.


**Choose the account structure first and the payment identifier second.** Otherwise, you risk solving incoming-payment matching while leaving treasury, audit, or counterparty requirements unresolved.


04


## Virtual IBANs: useful for identifying incoming payments


A virtual IBAN can act as a distinct collection identifier. When a payment arrives, the provider uses that identifier to attribute the receipt to the relevant customer or ledger balance. This reduces reliance on the payer entering an invoice reference correctly.


For example, you can ask whether separate customer identifiers all feed the same underlying collection account. That is a structure to investigate, not an assumption to make about every provider.


**Best for: businesses that need to distinguish incoming receipts.** The benefit is payment attribution; the limitation is that a distinct identifier does not necessarily create a distinct account, segregated balance, or independent legal claim against a bank.


Before issuing the details to customers, confirm the beneficiary name they should enter. Also establish what happens when the payer’s bank checks that name, requests supporting documents, or returns a payment. Do not substitute your preferred trading name for the provider’s documented instructions.


05


## Directly held bank accounts: useful when ownership is required


A directly held business bank account creates an account relationship between the named business and the bank. Its agreement specifies the account holder and applicable terms. That relationship is different from receiving an identifier through a payment provider.


**Best for: businesses whose counterparties require an account held in the business’s name.** The benefit is clearer evidence of the direct account relationship; the limitation is that the relationship alone does not establish support for every currency, collection method, or payment rail.


A bank account is not automatically the better operational choice for every collection workflow. You still need to check incoming-payment identification, outgoing-payment permissions, statements, and reconciliation support. Account ownership answers a legal question, not every operational question.


06


## Why virtual IBAN arrangements vary


“Virtual IBAN” does not describe a single legal or operational arrangement. For your 2026 evaluation, compare the contractual details rather than treating the label as a product specification.


- **Account holder:** Establish whether the underlying account names your business, the provider, or another entity.
- **Provider status:** Identify whether your contract is with a bank, payment institution, electronic money institution, or another service provider.
- **Funds treatment:** Determine whether the arrangement involves bank deposits, safeguarded customer funds, or another documented structure.
- **Payment permissions:** Check whether the identifier supports receiving only or also supports outgoing transactions and other payment functions.
- **Jurisdiction:** Identify the rules governing the provider, underlying account, customer eligibility, and any protection arrangement.
- **Recordkeeping:** Confirm how the provider records your entitlement and reconciles its customer ledger against underlying funds.


A provider’s answer should name the relevant entity and document. A statement that the service is “regulated” does not answer who owes your business the money or what happens if that entity fails.


07


## How do you check what a virtual IBAN actually gives you?


Use this sequence before replacing existing bank details. For a 2026 procurement decision, save the answers alongside the signed agreement so your finance and compliance teams work from the same account description.


1. **Account holder.** Ask for the legal name of the underlying account holder and a document establishing your business’s relationship to that account. Distinguish an account confirmation from a letter confirming only that an identifier is assigned to you.
2. **Funds location.** Ask which institution holds the funds and how the provider records your entitlement. If customer money is pooled, establish how the provider distinguishes your balance from other customers’ balances.
3. **Payment permissions.** Request written confirmation of supported incoming and outgoing payment types, currencies, beneficiary requirements, and restrictions. Do not treat successful receipt of a transfer as proof that outgoing payments are enabled.
4. **Failure treatment.** Ask what happens if the provider fails and what happens if the institution holding the funds fails. These are separate questions and can involve different recovery processes.
5. **Reconciliation test.** Trace a permitted test payment from the sender’s instruction through the transaction record, customer ledger, and statement. Verify that your team can identify the payer and match the receipt without manual guesswork.


*Check the underlying account relationship before relying on the payment identifier.*


The strongest evidence is a consistent set of documents: the agreement names the relationship, the funds explanation identifies the holding structure, and the transaction records show how payments reach your balance. If those descriptions conflict, resolve the conflict before distributing the details.


08


## Does a valid IBAN prove that you have a bank account?


**A valid IBAN proves neither account ownership nor deposit protection.** Format validation checks the identifier’s structure; it does not verify your contractual rights or confirm that a recipient can accept a particular payment.


The ISO 13616 IBAN format allows up to **34 alphanumeric characters** . It starts with **2 country-code letters** , followed by **2 check digits** , then the country-specific basic bank account number. The SWIFT IBAN Registry documents national IBAN formats.


Those structural rules explain why a virtual IBAN can look like other bank details. They do not classify the account holder’s legal relationship. For a 2026 account check, treat format validation, beneficiary verification, and account documentation as separate controls.


The same distinction applies to a country prefix. It identifies the IBAN’s country format; it does not, by itself, establish that your business has a local presence or that its funds qualify for a particular protection scheme.


09


## Can you send and receive money with a virtual IBAN?


**Receiving capability does not establish sending capability.** A virtual IBAN used for collections can identify incoming payments while outgoing payments operate through a separate account or provider workflow. Your agreement must specify the supported functions.


Ask about the transactions your business actually needs: customer receipts, supplier payments, refunds, direct debits, or transfers between your own accounts. Request confirmation for each relevant function rather than asking whether the service is “a full account.”


For a 2026 rollout, test the complete workflow, including exceptions. A receipt that reconciles correctly does not prove that a refund will reach the original payer or that an outgoing transfer will display your business as the sender. Confirm those behaviors separately.


10


## Is money behind a virtual IBAN protected like a bank deposit?


**A virtual IBAN does not establish deposit-insurance coverage.** Protection follows the legal arrangement, not the identifier displayed in your dashboard. A bank deposit and safeguarded payment-service funds involve different protection mechanisms.


Deposit insurance applies under the relevant scheme’s eligibility and coverage rules. Safeguarding generally concerns keeping eligible customer funds separate from the provider’s own funds through prescribed arrangements; it is not interchangeable with deposit insurance.


Ask for the applicable scheme or safeguarding explanation in writing. If coverage depends on an underlying bank or customer-level records, request the conditions that must be satisfied. Do not accept a bank’s name in a sales presentation as proof that your particular balance is insured.


11


## Where Infinite fits in a business banking review


**Infinite is for global businesses that need multicurrency accounts and cross-border payment routing.** Its financial platform provides USD and multicurrency bank accounts, compliance/KYB screening, and routing across SWIFT, ACH, Fedwire, and RTP, with settlement via stablecoins.


That scope is relevant when your requirement extends beyond identifying incoming receipts. It does not, by itself, answer the virtual-IBAN ownership question. Evaluate Infinite business accounts using the same account-holder, funds-treatment, and payment-permission checks you apply to any provider.


The distinction matters because payment routing and account ownership solve different problems. A supported payment rail describes how a transaction moves; the account agreement establishes the relationship governing the balance. Do not use either as a substitute for the other.


12


## FAQ


**Is a virtual IBAN the same as a real bank account?**


No—a virtual IBAN is not, by itself, a separate bank account. It can identify payments routed to an underlying account, while the agreement determines ownership and your rights to the funds.


**Can my business receive customer payments through a virtual IBAN?**


Yes, a virtual IBAN can identify incoming customer payments when the provider supports that collection function. Confirm supported currencies, payment types, and the exact beneficiary details before sharing it.


**Does having my company name on a virtual IBAN mean I own the account?**


No—displaying your company name does not establish ownership of the underlying account. Obtain documentation identifying the legal account holder and explaining your contractual relationship.


**Is a virtual IBAN better than a bank account for reconciliation?**


A virtual IBAN can improve payment attribution by assigning a distinct identifier to a customer or collection purpose. That operational benefit does not establish that it is a better place to hold funds.


**Does a virtual IBAN include deposit insurance?**


A virtual IBAN does not automatically include deposit insurance. Coverage depends on the institution, account structure, jurisdiction, eligibility rules, and any conditions applying to the arrangement.


**Can I use a virtual IBAN to make supplier payments?**


Only if the provider supports outgoing supplier payments under your account arrangement. An identifier assigned for incoming collections does not establish that capability.


**Does Infinite provide multicurrency business accounts?**


Infinite provides USD and multicurrency bank accounts for global businesses, alongside compliance/KYB screening and cross-border payment routing. Confirm the specific account structure and supported workflow during your evaluation.


13


## One last thing


**Ask for an account-ownership document before asking for more payment identifiers.** It forces the central distinction into the open: whether your business holds an account or uses details attached to another account arrangement.


Then give the document to whoever must accept it—your auditor, payment partner, or finance team. Their requirement is the practical test. An identifier that receives money successfully still does not replace evidence of the account relationship they need.
